snippet.title: Midjourney breaks into ... healthcare? #AI #Medtech #MidjourneyMedical #Medicalbreakthrough
snippet.description:
Midjourney medical is a real thing now. The AI image company built a full-body ultrasound.

It is cheaper than an MRI and faster. They want to run a billion scans a year, and apparently it is built to feel like a trip to the spa. The whole thing came out of a 40-person team that funds itself off the image business.

Here is the part that gets me. The most interesting AI move of the week did not come from OpenAI or Anthropic. It came from the company you thought only made pictures.

That is the signal worth watching. Capability is leaking out of the big labs and into small teams that own their own money and pick their own problems. Watch where that goes next.

snippet.title: 🤯 Why Is The Sky Blue? (It's Not What You Think!)
snippet.description:
Everyone knows the sky is blue, but have you ever wondered *why*? 🤯 In this Quirble, we're diving into the simple yet mind-blowing science behind our wonderfully blue skies!

Sunlight actually contains all colors, making it white. But when it hits Earth's atmosphere, things get interesting! Tiny gas molecules and particles scatter the light in every direction. Here's the secret: **blue light, with its shorter wavelength, gets scattered much more effectively than other colors.** That's why, when you look up, your eyes primarily catch all that scattered blue light, making the sky appear, well, blue!

It's a fantastic example of everyday physics revealing the magic of our world!

Did this scientific explanation surprise you? Share your thoughts in the comments below! 👇

snippet.title: Every AI Agent Demo Stops at Email. I Pointed Mine at the Bills That Cost You Money.
snippet.description:

AI agents usually get rebuilt from scratch for every new job. Here's how to build one reusable AI agent for messy, high-trust paperwork -- insurance appeals, tax prep, and beyond.

My Links 🔗

👉🏻 TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@nate.b.jones

What's really happening when an AI agent becomes trustworthy enough for your insurance denial and your taxes?

The common story is that every hard job needs its own custom agent -- but the real question is what you build once and point at everything else.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on building one reusable agent for messy, high-trust paperwork:

 - Why email and calendar is the 101 where mistakes stay cheap
 - How one nine-step skeleton carries into a denied insurance claim
 - What a cited appeal packet must do, and never promise
 - Where the human approval gate stays locked, from email to taxes

Learn the pattern on low-stakes email, and the paperwork that actually costs you money gets cheaper to face, as long as the last decision stays yours.

snippet.title: Will Fable 5 kill jobs? #fable5 #fableisback #anthropic #futureofwork
snippet.description:
The only jobs this model actually kills are the ones with zero judgment, the pure-execution roles where nothing really gets decided and the work could honestly have been automated any time in the last ten years anyway.

Everything else still needs a person, because a model this capable does not run itself, and someone still has to aim it, feed it the right context, check what it produced, and own the result when it lands on someone's desk. That is not a smaller job than the one you have now, it is a different one, and it leans on exactly the kind of judgment the model cannot supply on its own.

So if your work carries real judgment, you are not the person who should be nervous about any of this, you are the person who gets to point the thing and decide what good actually looks like.

Good news since I made this, by the way: Fable 5 is back. The breakdown below went out before it got pulled, so a few of the details are dated now, but most of what is in there still holds up.

How to actually use it: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/p/claude-fable-5-how-to-use?r=1z4sm5&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&showWelcomeOnShare=true

Everything else still needs a person, because a model this capable does not run itself, and someone still has to aim it, feed it the right context, check what it produced, and own the result when it lands on someone's desk. That is not a smaller job than the one you have now, it is a different one, and it leans on exactly the kind of judgment the model cannot supply on its own.

So if your work carries real judgment, you are not the person who should be nervous about any of this, you are the person who gets to point the thing and decide what good actually looks like.

Good news since I made this, by the way: Fable 5 is back. The breakdown below went out before it got pulled, so a few of the details are dated now, but most of what is in there still holds up.

snippet.title: GLM 5.2 Is Free And Beats Claude On Most Work. So Why Can't Companies Switch?
snippet.description:
Full post: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/p/glm-5-2-context-lock-in?r=1z4sm5&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&showWelcomeOnShare=true

GLM 5.2 is a free, open-source model that often beats Claude on everyday work, yet companies still pay frontier prices. The real bottleneck is no longer the model call. It is the last mile around it: context, routing, and harnesses.

My Links 🔗
👉🏻 Newsletter: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/
👉🏻 X: https://x.com/natebjones
👉🏻 TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@nate.b.jones
👉🏻 Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/nate.b.jones

What's really happening when intelligence gets 98% cheaper but your company's context stays trapped?

The common story is that a cheaper, better model means you should switch, but the real question is whether you can move your context, not whether the model can answer your prompt.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on GLM 5.2 and the last mile of cheap AI:

 - Where GLM 5.2 can safely replace an expensive frontier model
 - Why switching models means replacing a whole work system, not a call
 - How Claude Tag turns your team's Slack context into a sticky harness
 - What builders and agencies can do to own the last mile

Cheap intelligence is real and it is here, but the edge in 2026 belongs to whoever can build the harness and keep their own context instead of renting it back from a frontier lab.
